scenes.title: The 4 Core Analytical Pillars: FLAGS, PENNANTS, WEDGES, RECTANGLES & MEASURED MOVES

beats.hindi_tts: Pillar one: 1. Flags and Pennants (Half-Mast Principle). Brief, high-velocity continuation formations lasting 1 to 3 weeks that represent the exact halfway midpoint of a steep, dynamic market impulse.

cards.title: 1. Flags and Pennants (Half-Mast Principle)
cards.desc: Brief, high-velocity continuation formations lasting 1 to 3 weeks that represent the exact halfway midpoint of a steep, dynamic market impulse.

cards.title: 2. The Volume Contraction Invariant
cards.desc: Volume must contract sharply during pattern formation as liquidity dries up, followed by an explosive volume surge on the decisive breakout.

cards.title: 3. Wedges (Slanted Against Trend)
cards.desc: Convergence between two trendlines that slants counter to the prevailing trend: a falling wedge in an uptrend is bullish; a rising wedge in a downtrend is bearish.

cards.title: 4. The Measured Move Rule (Swing Equality)
cards.desc: In major trend advances, the secondary corrective consolidation wave is followed by a second impulse advance of equal point distance (Wave 1 = Wave 2).

steps: 1. Flags and pennants are high-velocity continuation patterns that typically fly at 'half-mast'.
2. The pattern must be preceded by a steep, nearly vertical price advance (the flagpole) on heavy volume.
3. Formation duration is brief: flags typically resolve within one to three weeks in daily charts.
4. Volume must dry up noticeably during the flag pause; expanding volume inside the flag warns of failure.
5. The breakout from the flag must be accompanied by an explosive expansion in trading volume.
6. Falling wedges in an uptrend are bullish; rising wedges in a downtrend are bearish (wedges slant against trend).
7. The Measured Move rule: the second impulse leg of a major advance predictably equals the point distance of the first leg.
8. Upon breaking out of a rectangular trading range, former resistance becomes future support on pullbacks.
